title: Single-edge exclusions restore bounded cell-gain fits without a unique edge diagnosis in seven selected Allen mouse groups
abstract: We tested whether failures of a current-to-voltage cell-gain model identify specific connections in Allen cortical slices. We used the paired amplitudes and selection from a prior signed study. At an assumed independent factor 1.10 error bound on each amplitude, five mouse inhibitory groups and two mouse excitatory groups failed the model. Exhaustive search found that one edge exclusion restored fit in every failing group. Each group had two to six alternative minimum repairs. No edge was present in every repair. In six groups every minimum repair removed all cycle constraints; in one inhibitory group a constraint remained. At zero tolerance, the nine testable mouse groups needed eleven exclusions in total. No human group was testable. These are conditional sensitivity and diagnosis results for released fits. They do not identify faulty measurements or biological mechanisms. Sparse slice graphs, missing paired measurements and assumed errors limit general use. Code, aggregate results, a figure, source hashes and external retrieval steps support reproduction.

display.caption: At an assumed factor 1.10 bound on each amplitude, seven selected mouse groups fail the gain model. Every group has multiple single-edge repairs. Only one group has a minimum repair that retains a cycle test. No edge occurs in every minimum repair.

citations.reason: Extends the paired-mode gain study to exhaustive minimum exclusions and diagnosis. Reuses its baseline-licensed SQL and linear program functions.
Prior target-only order comparison provides context.
